title: Power Automate process mining: import star schema (normalised) event data
summary: The briefing passes: the import workflow, storage prerequisites, licensing figures and Fabric controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes the launched roadmap status from Learn's preview label. One minor correction remains: the checklist asks administrators to check an environment prerequisite without a corresponding controls row.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Normalized import reads a star schema with a thin event table and optional case and lookup tables linked by foreign keys instead of requiring a flattened event table.
claims.quote: Instead of flattening everything in your lakehouse into one CSV, you can point Process Mining directly at a star schema—a thin event table plus optional case and lookup tables, linked by foreign keys.

claims.claim: The documented storage backends for normalized import are OneLake/Fabric and Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2.
claims.quote: It declares the storage backend (ADLS Gen2 or OneLake), the file format (CSV, Parquet, or Delta-Parquet), and a list of datasets.

claims.claim: Normalized import supports CSV, Parquet and Delta-Parquet formats.
claims.quote: | File formats | CSV, Parquet, Delta-Parquet | CSV, Parquet, Delta-Parquet |

claims.claim: The normalized-import UX guide lists managed Delta tables and loose Parquet or CSV files under a OneLake lakehouse's Files/ area.
claims.quote: OneLake / Microsoft Fabric: A lakehouse with managed Delta tables, or loose Parquet or CSV files under the Files/ area.

claims.claim: The normalized-import UX guide lists an ADLS Gen2 container with CSV, Parquet or Delta-Parquet folders.
claims.quote: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2: A container with CSV, Parquet, or Delta-Parquet folders.

claims.claim: A JSON configuration describes the tables, storage backend and mappings to Process Mining attributes.
claims.quote: A JSON config file describing your tables and how they map to Process Mining attributes.
